blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 27 in June to 32 in October (+18.5%), and it took 8.9% of the city’s 247 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 9 in June to 7 in October (−22.2%), and it took 3.9% of the city’s 230 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Northwest for detached houses in June (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, July (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: What buyers paid in Northwest Maple Ridge, November 2025 to October 2026 (Paragon closed sales)
The middle half of the 40 houses that closed in Northwest Maple Ridge sold between $1.15M and $1.35M. Typically they had 4 bedrooms, a build year around 1987 and a lot of about 7,338 square feet.
For houses in Northwest Maple Ridge that meant a median 16 days on the market, 97.1% of the asking price, 2% going over asking and about $487 a square foot of living space.

Quarter by quarter, the typical house in Northwest Maple Ridge went for $1.19M in November to January, $1.29M in February to April and $1.24M in May to July. February to April was the firmest stretch and November to January the softest.

The middle half of the 9 townhomes that closed in Northwest Maple Ridge sold between $590,000 and $675,000. The typical one had 3 bedrooms, a build year around 1986 and a strata fee near $479 a month.
For townhomes in Northwest Maple Ridge that meant a median 13 days on the market, 95.5% of the asking price, 0% going over asking and about $509 a square foot of living space.
6 condos closed in Northwest Maple Ridge, at a typical $481,500. The typical one had 2 bedrooms, a build year around 2004 and a strata fee near $440 a month.
For condos in Northwest Maple Ridge that meant a median 44 days on the market, 95.4% of the asking price, 0% going over asking and about $487 a square foot of living space.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: SD42 has no middle tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grades 8 to 12.

Transit, parks and health: Maple Meadows Station serves Maple Ridge's west side and Port Haney Station, 22300 River Road, runs weekday West Coast Express trains between Waterfront (downtown Vancouver) and Mission City. TransLink's Langley–Haney Place BRT is in detailed planning (22 km, Willowbrook to Haney Place), with designs, costs and timelines not yet determined. Nearest hospital: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge, with 24/7 emergency care.

Flood frame: the City publishes North and South Alouette River and Fraser River floodplain maps, and the Fraser River flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), with no habitable floor space below that level on affected lots and rental accommodation (suites) prohibited on floodplain properties under Zoning Bylaw s.402.8(h).
Suites and small-scale multi-unit housing follow Maple Ridge’s citywide rules; see the
The dated facts that are settled are the November 25, 2025 OCP updates and the October 28, 2025 Albion Area Plan adoption (Albion ground only).

blocks.text: Sources for what’s nearby
Northwest Maple Ridge: streets and boundaries

items.t: Northwest Maple Ridge has no City-published boundary; it is the board sub-area "Northwest" on Maple Ridge's west side.
Laity Street is the main north-south spine, with 123 Avenue and 124 Avenue running east-west through the housing.

blocks.text: Northwest Maple Ridge: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is mainly freehold detached houses on RS-1 lots, with a small attached pocket near Lougheed Highway.
Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 sets RS-1 subdivision minimums at 668.0 square metres area, 18.0 metres width and 27.0 metres depth, with 40% maximum lot coverage.
Infill lots on Hartnell Avenue show the current build form here: new detached houses on subdivided RS-1 lots, not strata product.

blocks.text: Northwest Maple Ridge: rules that affect buyers

items.t: No neighbourhood area plan covers the northwest housing area; the Official Community Plan (OCP) governs, updated November 25, 2025.

blocks.text: Northwest Maple Ridge: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Maple Meadows Station, not Port Haney, is the practical West Coast Express station for most northwest addresses.
Route 744 runs Meadowtown to Haney Place via 123 Avenue, Laity Street and 207 Street, linking the area to both stations and the Town Centre exchange.
Route 701 runs from Coquitlam Central Station via Maple Meadows Station and Haney Place along the Lougheed corridor south of the area.
Merkley Park is listed by the City at 22008 124 Avenue; an earlier City page gave a different address, so confirm the park entrance by street, not by memory.
Ridge Meadows Hospital at 11666 Laity Street is in this quadrant of the city, on Laity Street itself.
SD42 has no middle school tier, so children move from a Kindergarten to Grade 7 elementary school directly to a Grade 8 to 12 secondary school.

blocks.text: Northwest Maple Ridge: development and new projects

items.t: The Abernethy Way widening west phases are complete to 232 Street, which changes east-west trips from the northwest side, with the 232 to 240 Street phase starting construction in 2027.

blocks.text: Northwest Maple Ridge: getting around

items.t: West Coast Express from Maple Meadows Station is the rapid transit here, running weekday trains between Waterfront and Mission City.
Haney Place is the bus exchange for the area, served by routes 701, 743 and 744 on the Laity Street and Lougheed corridors.

blocks.text: Northwest Maple Ridge: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the City floodplain maps for the exact lot before removing subjects, because the Fraser River flood construction level is 6.7 metres geodetic on affected lots.
The floodplain maps do not set a suite value: suites are prohibited on floodplain properties, so a below-grade suite on a low lot needs a separate bylaw check.
